en: Clouds over Mount Mayon contain tiny liquid water droplets and solid ice crystals, not just water vapor.
Muddy water from the Pasig River is a suspension where solid dirt particles settle at the bottom over time.
Rusty gates in coastal Batangas undergo a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form iron oxide.
Shaved ice in halo-halo undergoes a physical change from solid to liquid when left out in the tropical heat.
Pumice stones from Taal Volcano float on water because their porous structure makes them less dense than liquid water.
Sugar dissolves completely in hot calamansi juice to form a clear solution because higher temperatures increase the sugar's solubility.
Helium balloons at a Manila fiesta rise into the air because helium gas is less dense than the surrounding atmospheric air.
Sea salt harvested in Zambales is left behind when seawater undergoes evaporation, a physical change from liquid to gas.
Steaming puto in bamboo steamers involves a chemical change where heat causes the rice flour batter to permanently solidify.
Fresh carabao milk is a colloid where tiny liquid fat droplets are evenly dispersed throughout the watery liquid.
Iron-rich black sand on Ilocos beaches is strongly attracted to magnets due to its high magnetite mineral content.
Water droplets on a cold glass of buko juice show condensation, where water vapor in the air cools into liquid.
